candidates.source_name: CBCG — Radne studije (Central Bank of Montenegro Working Paper series)
candidates.why_relevant: The central bank's own research department (Sektor za istraživanja i statistiku) publishes analytical working papers as free PDFs. Series confirmed to include financial-market, banking-sector, COVID-19 banking and credit/deposit analyses; the natural home for any CBCG analysis of payment habits, card usage or cash demand that is not in statistical releases.
candidates.access_status: open, free PDFs, no registration observed
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic HTML scrape of the index page for new PDF links; download and text-extract PDFs; diff against stored inventory
queries_used: CBCG radne studije working paper platni promet kartice Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: CBCG Radna studija br. 10 — Analiza finansijskog tržišta u Crnoj Gori (PDF exemplar)
candidates.why_relevant: Concrete exemplar of the CBCG working-paper PDF pattern; useful to pin the URL template (/slike_i_fajlovi/fajlovi/fajlovi_publikacije/radne_studije/<slug>.pdf) for systematic harvesting of the whole series.
candidates.access_status: open PDF
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Direct PDF download + text extraction; use as URL-template seed
candidates.discovered_via_method: search result snowball from working-paper index
queries_used: CBCG radne studije working paper platni promet kartice Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: Montenegrin Journal of Economics (MNJE) — ELIT, Podgorica
candidates.why_relevant: Peer-reviewed, Scopus-indexed (Q1 SJR reported) open-access economics journal published from Podgorica by NGO 'Economic Laboratory for Transition Research' (ELIT). Regional venue where Montenegrin and Western-Balkan authors publish empirical banking, fintech-adoption and payment-behaviour studies with survey microdata.
candidates.access_status: open access
candidates.legal_status: open-access scholarly publication; respect journal licence for redistribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl issue archive; alternatively harvest via DOAJ API (ISSN 1800-6698 / 1800-5845) and filter abstracts on payment/card/bank keywords
queries_used: "Montenegrin Journal of Economics" payments cards banking digital adoption

candidates.source_name: DOAJ listing for Montenegrin Journal of Economics (metadata pointer)
candidates.why_relevant: Machine-readable article metadata/abstract feed for MNJE, letting keyword monitoring run without scraping the journal site.
candidates.access_status: open, public API
candidates.suggested_collection_method: DOAJ public search API polling by ISSN with keyword filters
queries_used: "Montenegrin Journal of Economics" payments cards banking digital adoption

candidates.source_name: Univerzitet Crne Gore — Ekonomski fakultet Podgorica (Faculty of Economics)
candidates.why_relevant: Oldest and largest Montenegrin economics faculty; staff research, conference proceedings and student/staff theses are the main domestic academic producer of survey-based work on payment behaviour and banking. Faculty pages carry announcements, projects and publication lists.
candidates.access_status: open; site structure is CMS-driven and partly JS-rendered
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl faculty publications/announcements sections; supplement with site: queries in Serbian/Montenegrin
queries_used: Ekonomski fakultet Podgorica istraživanje bezgotovinsko plaćanje kartice

candidates.source_name: UCG institutional repository / 'skladiste' document store (theses and dissertations)
candidates.why_relevant: University of Montenegro hosts full-text doctoral dissertations and master theses as PDFs under /skladiste/. Confirmed to host at least one banking/finance dissertation (Đurović, on national development and financial institutions). Theses frequently contain original merchant/consumer surveys and reconstructed card/POS series unavailable elsewhere.
candidates.access_status: open PDFs; no unified search index observed — discovery via site: queries
candidates.legal_status: public academic works; author copyright applies to reuse
candidates.suggested_collection_method: site:ucg.ac.me filetype:pdf keyword sweeps (kartično poslovanje, platni promet, bezgotovinsko, POS terminali) plus direct PDF fetch
queries_used: ISSP Institut za strateške studije i projekcije Crna Gora istraživanje banke finansije

candidates.source_name: ISSP — Institut za strateške studije i projekcije (Institute for Strategic Studies and Prognoses), Podgorica
candidates.why_relevant: Montenegro's best-known independent economic think tank; runs its own recurring surveys, built the macroeconomic model of Montenegro, and its researchers comment publicly on bank interest rates and financial sector conditions. Has a downloadable publications section.
candidates.access_status: open publications download endpoint observed (/en/publications/download-publication/<id>)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate publications listing, fetch download-publication PDFs, filter on financial/payments keywords
queries_used: ISSP Institut za strateške studije i projekcije Crna Gora istraživanje banke finansije
local_language_terms_used: Institut za strateške studije i projekcije

candidates.source_name: DeFacto Consultancy (Podgorica) — market research and public-opinion agency
candidates.why_relevant: Described as the largest Montenegrin market-research and public-opinion agency; the most likely domestic fieldwork contractor behind bank/card/consumer-payment surveys (client-commissioned, occasionally published or press-released). Key actor to track for survey existence even when microdata is proprietary.
candidates.access_status: public website; most research is client-confidential
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor news/projects pages and LinkedIn/Facebook posts for released survey headlines; contact for syndicated reports

candidates.why_relevant: Leading Montenegrin business-consulting firm explicitly serving banking clients; produces sector studies, feasibility work and SME surveys that occasionally quantify merchant acceptance and financing behaviour.
candidates.access_status: public site; deliverables largely client-owned

queries_used: CEED Consulting De Facto Consultancy Ipsos Crna Gora istraživanje tržišta banke

candidates.source_name: Bankar.me — Montenegrin banking analysis portal
candidates.why_relevant: Publishes recurring quantitative analyses of Montenegrin bank performance ('Analiza poslovanja banaka u Crnoj Gori', annual and half-yearly), reprocessing CBCG data into sector-level metrics. A de-facto analyst layer between raw regulator statistics and market conclusions, and a good pointer to who else is analysing the sector.
candidates.access_status: open web
candidates.legal_status: copyrighted editorial content — index and cite, do not republish
candidates.suggested_collection_method: RSS/category crawl of the banking analysis category; scheduled fetch of 'Analiza poslovanja banaka' series

candidates.source_name: UBCG — Udruženje banaka Crne Gore, magazine 'Bankar'
candidates.why_relevant: The banking association's decade-old professional journal 'Bankar' carries semi-academic articles by bank practitioners and academics on payment systems, card business and digitalisation; issues are posted as full PDFs (e.g. Bankar 38).

candidates.why_relevant: Aggregates full text of regional social-science journals including Montenegrin/Serbian publishers; the most efficient way to find local-language academic articles on payment behaviour that never surface in Google Scholar.

candidates.legal_status: licensed content — metadata harvesting only unless subscribed

candidates.why_relevant: Montenegro's main private university, with international-economics/finance and information-systems faculties (FIST) that supervise master theses on digital banking and payments; thesis rules and some works are posted on faculty subdomains.

candidates.why_relevant: The only internationally comparable demand-side survey covering account ownership, digital payments, card use and cash reliance; Montenegro is among the 141 economies in the 2025 round (~145,000 adults). Microdata catalogue entry allows respondent-level analysis of cash-preference and digital-adoption for ME.
candidates.access_status: open; microdata catalogue may require a free account and stated purpose
candidates.legal_status: open data under World Bank terms of use
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download country-level indicator CSVs from the Findex download-data page; request Montenegro microdata via microdata.worldbank.org catalogue 7860
candidates.discovered_via_method: English-language cross-check of demand-side survey sources

candidates.legal_status: press content; survey IP belongs to Visa

negative_findings.description: No CBCG working paper (Radna studija) specifically about payment systems, card usage, POS/ATM networks or cash demand was identified in the visible series index.
negative_findings.result_summary: The Radne studije index lists inflation, climate, public debt, tourism, real estate, FDI, credit/deposit and COVID-banking topics; the fetched page exposed titles and PDF links but no authors/years, and nothing payments-specific surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's highest-value hypothesis — that CBCG researchers publish payment-behaviour analysis outside statistical releases — is not confirmed; A4 payment analysis may instead live in the Financial Stability Report or Godišnji izvještaj rather than the working-paper series.

negative_findings.description: No published Faculty of Economics Podgorica study on cashless payment / card adoption was found via local-language search.
negative_findings.result_summary: Serbian-language query 'Ekonomski fakultet Podgorica istraživanje bezgotovinsko plaćanje kartice' returned only institutional pages (ucg.ac.me/ef, programme lists, social media) and no research output.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests domestic academic payment research is either unindexed, published in Serbian-language journals off the open web, or embedded in theses — requiring repository sweeps rather than search-engine discovery.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegro-specific article from the Montenegrin Journal of Economics on payments/cards/digital adoption was surfaced in this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: The journal itself was confirmed (mnje.com, ISSN 1800-6698/1800-5845, ELIT Podgorica) but the search returned only non-Montenegrin digital-payments literature.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Article-level discovery for this journal needs the DOAJ/Scopus index or the journal archive rather than general web search; do not conclude the journal lacks relevant papers.

negative_findings.description: Domestic commercial survey work (DeFacto, CEED, Ipsos Adria) appears to be client-confidential with no public report library.
negative_findings.result_summary: Company profiles and directory entries were found, but no downloadable banking/payments studies.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Merchant/consumer survey evidence for ME likely exists but is only reachable via press releases or direct commercial contact — collection method must be relationship-based, not scraping.

negative_findings.description: No page in this slice was fetched-and-confirmed beyond the CBCG working-paper index; all other URLs come from search-result metadata.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only https://www.cbcg.me/me/publikacije/ostale-publikacije/radne-studije was retrieved directly; the rest are unverified candidate URLs.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Liveness must be established by the deterministic verification pass; confidence scores here reflect provenance quality, not reachability.

coverage_gaps.description: Regional/IFI research producers that routinely cover Western Balkan payments (EBRD BEEPS merchant surveys, IMF Article IV and FSAP selected issues, EIB CESEE Bank Lending Survey, Vienna Initiative, wiiw) were not yet searched for their Montenegro cuts.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated sweep of EBRD/IMF/EIB/wiiw/World Bank Western Balkans Regular Economic Report for ME payment and financial-inclusion chapters.

coverage_gaps.description: Scholar-level indexes (Google Scholar, Scopus, CrossRef, CONOR/COBISS.CG national bibliography) were not queried for Montenegrin-authored payment papers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query COBISS.CG and CrossRef for sr-language titles containing platni promet, kartično poslovanje, bezgotovinsko plaćanje, digitalno bankarstvo restricted to ME institutions.

coverage_gaps.description: Montenegrin-Latin variants and transliteration alternatives (kartično poslovanje, POS terminali, bankomati, digitalizacija plaćanja, instant plaćanja) were only partly exercised; Cyrillic variants were not used at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Repeat searches with the extended glossary and with Cyrillic spellings (платни промет, готовина, картице) to catch Serbian-hosted regional research.

coverage_gaps.description: No academic or consultancy source specifically analysing ATM/POS network economics or acceptance-network density in Montenegro was located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Target scheme/processor-adjacent analysis (Visa/Mastercard economic institutes, Allied Wallet-style processor whitepapers, regional processors) and CBCG payment-system statistics commentary.

coverage_gaps.description: UCG repository content has no discoverable unified search interface; thesis discovery depended on incidental search hits.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test for an OAI-PMH/DSpace endpoint at UCG and check the national ETD portal; otherwise build a site:-query sweeper over ucg.ac.me/skladiste with the payments glossary.

brief: Montenegro's analytical layer for payments is thin and concentrated: the CBCG's own 'Radne studije' series is the single most credible domestic research channel, but its visible catalogue is macro/inflation/climate-oriented with no payments-specific paper identified, so the richest analyst-grade evidence is likely to sit in international demand-side surveys (World Bank Global Findex 2025, which covers Montenegro) and in scheme-commissioned consumer research (Visa Pulse) that reaches the public only through Montenegrin media. Domestic academia contributes through the Podgorica-based, Scopus-indexed Montenegrin Journal of Economics (ELIT), the University of Montenegro Faculty of Economics and its PDF thesis store, and UDG — all of which need repository- and index-level sweeps rather than web search, since no faculty payment study surfaced in local-language queries. The think-tank/consultancy tier (ISSP, DeFacto, CEED) plus the UBCG journal 'Bankar' and the bankar.me analysis series form a practitioner analysis layer that reprocesses CBCG data and occasionally runs original fieldwork, though commercial survey output is client-confidential. Highest-value next moves are IFI Montenegro cuts (EBRD/IMF/EIB/wiiw) and bibliographic-index sweeps in Serbian, including Cyrillic.
